title: Garden and Spire Again
premise: Felix Yarrow, the last apprentice of the Ledgerkeepers—a guild that trades in impossible things—discovers that the guild's founding contract holds the key to the fallen border wards: the stars went out because someone has been quietly selling starlight, and the buyer means to unmake the old truce between human and fae realms. Hunted by a corrupt royal inquisitor who wants the contract destroyed and by a fae emissary who wants it weaponized, Felix must choose between the guild's law of neutrality and their own hunger for justice. In the end, Felix burns the contract's binding clause to relight the stars, dissolving the guild's power forever but forging a new, honest covenant between realms—with Felix as its first witness rather than its master.
about_author: Dominic Zhou is a former archivist who writes fantasies about the people who keep records of magic rather than wield it. They live in a rainy coastal city with two cats and an ever-growing collection of unread field guides.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. During the guild's annual audit, Felix notices entries for starlight sold in impossible quantities—then the border wards fail and the stars die overhead. The guild master is found dead, the ledgers stolen, and Felix escapes with the founding contract. The emotional beat is shock curdling into resolve: the quiet clerk realizes the guild's secrets are now their burden alone.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Ash
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, with interludes from the inquisitor Serah Vane. Pursued through the capital's undercity, Felix bargains with smugglers and discovers Vane has been buying the stolen starlight to fund her private war on the fae. An old smuggler ally is burned alive as a warning. The beat is fear sharpened by grief—Felix learns neutrality protects no one.

chapters.title: The Emissary's Bargain
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Cornered by the fae emissary Ithuriel, Felix is offered a tempting deal: help weaponize the contract against the humans who betrayed the truce, and be granted a true place among the fae—the belonging Felix has never had. Torn, Felix nearly accepts, until they realize Ithuriel's victory would simply replace one corrupt power with another. The beat is temptation and the cost of saying no.

chapters.title: Witness
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, converging with Vane and Ithuriel at the ruined ward-spire. In the climax, Felix refuses both hunters and burns the contract's binding clause, feeding the guild's hoarded starlight back into the sky; the stars reignite as the guild's vault collapses. Vane is arrested by her own officers, Ithuriel departs bound by the new open covenant, and Felix, guild-less but free, signs the first honest ledger. The beat is grief transmuted into chosen belonging.
